transcript.text: my belling cooker keeps burnin stuff 1 day then next day its undercookd on same temp. been like it a cuple months. thermastat??

To answer your question: on modern electronic cookers there isn't a traditional 'thermostat' you can just swap out; instead, the oven uses an internal temperature sensor and a control board to manage heat. On older dial-controlled models, it would be a mechanical thermostat. The fact that it alternates between burning and undercooking suggests the appliance is struggling to regulate its own temperature accurately. This could be due to a failing temperature sensor (which tells the oven how hot it is) or a drifting thermostat, but we need to know what kind of control you have first. Does your cooker have a digital display with buttons, or is it controlled by physical dials/knobs?
its got knobs, the old fashioned kind, and a little orange light that comes on. no digital screen or anything. its a double oven, the main one is the one thats gone funny, the top one seems fine

With mechanical knobs and an indicator light, your cooker relies on a physical thermostat to switch the heating elements on and off to maintain temperature. The fact that it alternates between burning and undercooking suggests this thermostat is 'drifting'—meaning it thinks the oven is hotter than it actually is (causing it to cut the heat too early) or vice versa. Before we consider replacing parts, let's check if the heating element itself is working properly. Could you set the main oven to 180°C on a standard bake function and leave it for about 10 minutes? Once it's been on for a while, carefully look through the glass door (or feel the air coming out if safe) — does the heating element at the back glow bright red, or is it barely warm/dim?

ok i put it on 180 but i cant really see any element in the main oven, its a fan one so its all behind a metal panel at the back i think. i cant tell if its glowing or not sorry. i dont have an oven thermometer either. what else can i check??

Since you can't see the element behind the panel, we need to check if the oven is actually getting hot. Please set the main oven to 180°C on a standard fan bake function (usually shown as a fan inside a circle) and leave it for about 20 minutes. After that time, carefully place your hand near the door opening (without touching any internal parts) — does the air feel warm/hot, or is it still cool? Also, watch the orange light: does it stay on continuously while heating, or does it flicker on and off as if cycling?

ok i did it. the orange light goes off after about 10 mins sometimes, but other times it seems to stay on for ages. the fan i can hear going i think. havent really done the hand bit properly yet sorry, is that important?

Yes, that is very important. The orange light cycling tells us how the oven is behaving: if it stays on for ages, the oven is running hotter than the thermostat thinks (which explains why you are burning things). If it cuts off after 10 minutes but the food isn't cooked, the thermostat is cutting the heat too early. To find the right replacement part for your Belling cooker, I just need the model number. Could you look for a rating plate or sticker on the frame around the oven door opening (or inside the door seal) and tell me what it says?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
i cant find any sticker, ive looked round the door frame and theres nothing there. all i know is its a belling, 60cm, double oven. will that do? and do i still need to do the hand bit?

The '60cm double oven' description isn't enough for me to identify the exact part you need, as Belling made many different models with that size. However, I can still guide you through a check to confirm what's wrong. Yes, please do the hand test now. Set the main oven to 180°C on fan bake and wait about 20 minutes. This suggests if the oven is actually heating up at all. If it feels warm but you're still burning food, that points to a drifting thermostat (the part that tells the oven when to stop heating). If it stays cool, we have a different issue with the heating element.
ok ill do the hand bit now. the knob is a bit wobbly too, not sure if that matters. will let you know what it feels like

The wobbly knob is a useful clue—it suggests the mechanism controlling the temperature might be loose or worn. Since you can't find the label, please look inside the door seal of the top oven or on the side of the cooker frame near the hob; sometimes manufacturers put one sticker there even if they don't on the main door. If you still can't find it, take a photo of the control panel and the rating plate area to send to a parts supplier—they often recognise the model from photos. In the meantime, try using an oven thermometer (a cheap glass one) for your next bake.

ok i looked on the top oven door and the side of the frame and still no sticker anywhere, sorry. i dont have a thermometer either so cant do that bit. is there anything else i can check? the door seal on the main oven is a bit flattened at the top corner but the door shuts ok

Since you can't find the model number or use a thermometer right now, let's look at two things: heat loss and temperature control. A flattened seal (especially if it creates a gap) will make the oven work harder to stay hot, which can confuse the thermostat. Please check for light leaks around the door edges in a dark room. However, your main symptom—alternating between burning and undercooking on the same setting—is classic 'thermostat drift'. The mechanical thermostat inside is likely failing to switch the heating off at the right time. Because you can't identify the exact part without the model number, and this involves internal electrical components, I recommend getting a qualified engineer to check the oven thermostat/sensor assembly safely.

candidates: Faulty temperature sensor or control board (Electronic oven) (high)
